solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Roots and branch — or some part of it

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the run of words that follows, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A gardener talks about roots and a branch, or just a bit of one.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'brANCH OR Some', and 'part of it' tells you to take just that stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To root something is to fix it firmly in place, which is what anchoring it does: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Nothing more than water

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, meaning only or simply, as in a trifling amount
a small lake or pond, an old and poetic word for a body of water

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the adjective for only or simply; the other is the old noun for a lake or pond.

clue.text: Comments from assistants welcoming head of security

indicators.note: the helpers take in a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: aides are assistants

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Office assistants mutter remarks as the security chief arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives S, the first letter of 'security', and 'welcoming' puts it inside AIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks made in passing, often spoken so that only some can hear: a synonym for comments.

clue.text: Game for foundation degree students

parts.note: a base is a foundation
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
L is a learner, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: A sport suited to people studying for a foundation degree.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display; two of them stand for students.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is a bat-and-ball sport, an example of the general word for a sport or pastime.

clue.text: Leaving see, prepared to spread the word

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a fresh arrangement, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A missionary leaves the bishop's see, ready to preach the gospel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the letters of LEAVING SEE. A see is a bishop's diocese, which helps the churchy surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To evangelise is to preach the Christian gospel, literally spreading the good word to others.

clue.text: Confirm half of bets on a heavy defeat

indicators.note: only the first half of the word's four letters is used

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A punter splits stakes on a team suffering a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes BE, the front half of 'bets'; 'on' is just a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear out a claim is to support or corroborate it, a phrasal-verb synonym for confirm.

clue.text: Extreme case of indecision under stress

indicators.note: one piece sits beneath or comes before the other in the build
the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: to stress something is to tense it, put it under strain

explanation.surface: An extreme example of dithering while under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives IN, the outer letters of 'indecision'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means existing in a high or extreme degree, as in intense heat: an adjective synonym.

clue.text: In the main, forces welcome victory for workers

indicators.note: the fleets take a guest into their midst, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: forces at sea, the main being the ocean, are navies

explanation.surface: Out at sea, the armed forces cheer a victory for the working man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the open sea, so forces there are navies.
explanation.definitionFit: Navvies are labourers on roads, canals and railways, a particular kind of manual worker.

clue.text: A bit of chicken for the minister?

definitions.text: A bit of chicken for the minister?

parts.words: A bit of chicken for the minister?
parts.note: read as the cut of a roast bird reserved for a clergyman; in fact it is the fatty tail end of a cooked fowl

explanation.surface: Which portion of the roast chicken should go to the vicar?
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the name literally as a clergyman's portion; it is really the fleshy rump of a cooked bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the everyday name for the fatty tail of a cooked fowl, here imagined as a cleric's own cut.

clue.text: Well-worn bed, rather a mess!

indicators.note: the letters are put into disorder, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tatty old bed in rather a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' rearranges the letters of BED RATHER A.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare describes fabric worn so thin the threads show, the same as well-worn.

clue.text: Clumsy chap encountered during dinner date

indicators.note: the letters are met with in the middle of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An awkward man was met on a dinner date.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'dinNER Date'.
explanation.definitionFit: A socially awkward or inept man is commonly called a geek or dweeb, the slang sense here.

clue.text: Assumptions that come from building

definitions.meaning: propositions taken as true from which an argument proceeds

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the starting points of an argument; the other is a building with its land.

clue.text: Nocturnal climber scrambling from new loo

indicators.note: the letters are jumbled up, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A night-time climber clambers out of a newly installed toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambling' rearranges the letters of FROM NEW LOO. 'Climber' is a climbing plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a climbing plant whose white flowers open at night, so nocturnal climber describes it.

clue.text: Approach a goddess, finally changing direction

indicators.note: the last letter is a compass point which is swapped for another compass point

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love

explanation.surface: Someone approaches a goddess, who turns away at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally changing direction' swaps VENUS's last letter S (south) for E (east), giving VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a way of approaching something, literal or figurative, as in an avenue of inquiry.

clue.text: Song of genie hoarding two antiques

indicators.note: the genie keeps treasures stashed inside, so pieces go within it
the word tells you the old-thing piece goes in twice, at two separate spots

parts.note: an antique is something old
the second copy of the same old thing

explanation.surface: A tune about a genie who keeps a pair of antiques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarding' and 'two' together put OLD into GENIE twice, at separate spots: G-OLD-EN-OLD-IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden oldie is a song popular long ago and still well loved, so it is an example of a song.

clue.text: Reveal that day is nigh

parts.note: nigh means near or close

explanation.surface: Announce that the day of reckoning is near.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known something hidden, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Encourage one love for so long

parts.note: to cheer someone on is to encourage them
I is the Roman numeral one
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Give a loved one a boost before going away for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a length of time but is a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British farewell, just as so long is a casual goodbye.

clue.text: Warnings from speleologists having a time for reflection, initially

indicators.note: one set of letters stands in place of another

parts.note: speleologists explore caves, so they are cavers

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: Cave explorers issue warnings after pausing for thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R from 'reflection', and A plus T (time) replace it in CAVERS; 'having' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a cautionary proviso or qualification, a formal word for a warning.

clue.text: Dresses for work duties

definitions.meaning: periods of work in a rota, as in a night stint at the factory

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is simple straight-cut dresses; the other is set spells of work on a rota.

clue.text: He, for example, is the talk of the House of Lords!

parts.note: members of the House of Lords are peers, so noble
gas is idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a peer's speech as typical of the upper chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is not a man but the symbol for helium, an inert gas; the House of Lords is Britain's unelected upper chamber of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium, chemical symbol He, belongs to the inert family of elements in the periodic table's last column.

clue.text: Legislature loses heart following dollar's collapse

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the build

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar

indicators.note: the word's insides go, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A parliament is dispirited after the currency crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' leaves LE, the ends of 'legislature'.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle is to give way under pressure, bending or crumpling, the same as collapse.

clue.text: Check out oxygen bar

parts.note: to vet something is to check it out thoroughly
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Inspect an oxygen bar before going in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a verb meaning forbid, not a place to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is the right to forbid, and to veto something is to bar it.

clue.text: Fruitless campaigns, having mislaid bags outside university

parts.note: something mislaid is lost

indicators.note: the luggage sits around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: cases are bags or luggage

explanation.surface: Doomed missions, and someone has left their luggage outside the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts CASES around U.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is an effort or movement with no chance of success, so a fruitless campaign.

clue.text: Desire that Labour generally suppresses

indicators.note: the words hold the letters down inside them, concealing them

explanation.surface: An ambition that the Labour party usually stifles.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'laboUR GEnerally'.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong desire or impulse to do something, a noun synonym.

clue.text: To empower student, one needs logic, say

parts.note: L is a learner, so a student
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so its sound rather than its spelling is used

parts.note: sense is sound reasoning, logic

explanation.surface: To give a learner powers, they first need good reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: To license is to grant someone formal permission or authority, which is to empower them; the verb spelling ends -SE.

clue.text: Ruins Blackpool's first illuminations

indicators.note: only the first letter of the place name is taken

parts.note: illuminations are decorative lights

explanation.surface: The Blackpool Illuminations, the seaside town's first show, are spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool, a seaside resort in north-west England, is famous for its autumn Illuminations, a long display of lights along the seafront.
explanation.definitionFit: To blight something is to spoil or ruin it, as frost blights crops.
